residency.test: Resident if present 183 days in the tax year, or 280 days across the current and preceding year with at least 30 days in each.
residency.ordinary_residence: Acquired after three consecutive years of residence and retained for three years after leaving - a separate concept that catches many departing taxpayers.
residency.domicile: Non-domiciled residents are taxed on foreign income and gains only to the extent remitted to Ireland. This regime remains in place.

headline.rates: 20% up to the standard rate band, 40% above
headline.standard_rate_band: 44,000 single; 53,000 for a one-income married couple; up to 88,000 for two incomes
headline.usc: Universal Social Charge of 0.5% to 8% on gross income

married_joint.note: one-income couple band; a two-income couple can raise this to 88,000

credits.name: Employee (PAYE) tax credit
credits.note: not available to proprietary directors or the self-employed

employee.name: PRSI Class A
employee.note: exempt below 352 per week; a tapered credit applies just above that

employer.name: Employer PRSI
employer.note: 8.9% on weekly earnings below the lower threshold

capital_gains.deadlines: gains from January to November are paid by 15 December of the same year; December gains by 31 January

quirks: Tax credits reduce tax directly and are the main relief mechanism. Married couples should check that credits and the standard rate band are allocated between them in the way that minimises tax.
The USC is a separate charge on gross income with its own bands, and it applies to income that income tax reliefs have already sheltered.

Non-domiciled residents can use the remittance basis - Ireland retained it after the UK abolished its version in 2025, which has made Ireland notably more attractive for internationally mobile people.
Capital gains tax is paid on a self-assessed basis during the year of disposal, months before the return itself is due.
Most PAYE employees settle up through a simple Form 12 or an online statement of liability rather than a full self-assessment return.

reporting.portal: https://www.revenue.ie - myAccount for PAYE, ROS for self-assessed
reporting.who_must_file: Self-assessed taxpayers (the self-employed, company directors, landlords and those with substantial non-PAYE income) file a Form 11. PAYE-only taxpayers use myAccount to claim credits and get a Statement of Liability.

deadlines.what: Form 11 for 2025, plus preliminary tax for 2026
Extended deadline for filing and paying through ROS
CGT payment for disposals from January to November 2026
PAYE taxpayers can claim refunds for prior years

forms.name: Return for PAYE taxpayers with modest non-PAYE income
End of year PAYE reconciliation, requested in myAccount
Replaced the P60 - available in myAccount

documents_to_collect: PPS number and myAccount or ROS access
Employment Detail Summary for each employment
Medical expense receipts - 20% relief is available on most unreimbursed costs
Rent tax credit details and tenancy registration
Pension contribution certificates - age-related limits apply
Records of any foreign income and foreign tax paid

penalties.late_filing: 5% surcharge if filed within two months of the deadline, 10% after, capped at 63,485
penalties.late_payment: daily interest of about 0.0219% (roughly 8% a year)
penalties.preliminary_tax: interest applies where preliminary tax is less than 90% of the final liability or 100% of the prior year

sources.name: Revenue - Personal tax credits, reliefs and exemptions

warnings: USC bands are modelled as separate contributions; the 2% band ceiling and the third band floor should be checked against the current year's figures.
The married two-income standard rate band increase (up to 88,000) is not applied automatically - use the single status for each spouse where that is more accurate.
PRSI weekly thresholds and the tapered credit for low earners are not modelled.
